items.title: Power consumers may face Rs1.73/unit tariff hike
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Elec­tri­city consumers across the country may face a Rs1.73 per unit increase following a request to adjust power tariffs under the monthly fuel adjustment mechanism for August. The Central Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) has filed the application with the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority (Nepra), which will hear the request on Sept 29. The proposed increase will also apply to consumers of K-Electric (KE), according to the request. The CPPA said 14.464 billion units of electricity were supplied to distribution companies (Discos) in August at an average cost of Rs8.82 per unit. Generation mix Hydropower accounted for 37.84 per cent of total electricity generation during the month, while 10.88pc was generated from local coal and 15.59pc from imported coal. Electricity generated from furnace oil accounted for 2.15pc, while local gas contributed 7.04pc and imported LNG 8.48pc. The CPPA said the cost of electricity generated from furnace oil stood at Rs45.25 per unit, while power generated from imported LNG cost Rs45.92 per unit. Last month, Nepra approved an financial burden of about Rs9.8bn on electricity consumers by allowing a fuel cost adjustment of 75.03 paise per unit in August electricity bills. Nepra said it had decided that the positive FCA for June 2026, amounting to Rs0.7503 per kilowatt-hour, would be applicable to all consumer categories of KE and ex-Wapda distribution companies, except lifeline consumers, electric vehicle charging stations and pre-paid electricity consumers of all categories who had opted for the pre-paid tariff. The regulator had said the higher FCA would also apply to consumers under the incremental consumption package. Distribution companies and KE were directed to reflect the fuel cost adjustment for June this year in electricity bills issued for August. Published in Dawn, September 20th, 2026

items.title: Day First Lady commissioned ICT hub at Oko Polytechnic
items.description: By Chuks Okoye Recently, the Oko community, particularly the Federal Polytechnic, Oko, (OkoPoly), Anambra State, was agog with dignitaries, including the academics, captains of industries, politicians, businessmen and women, as well as students and Oko residents as the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, visited the polytechnic. Senator Tinubu was at the Polytechnic to inaugurate an ICT Experience Centre. The Anambra State Governor, Prof Chukwuma Soludo and his wife, as well as 16 other governors’ wives accompanied Mrs Tinubu to the event. Inaugurating the Centre, she said it was a major investment in the digital future of Nigerian youths, stressing that such facilities were essential to equipping young Nigerians with the competencies required to participate meaningfully in a rapidly changing global economy. According to the first Lady, the project also fits squarely into the mandate of a technical institution such as Federal Polytechnic Oko, where practical knowledge and industry-relevant skills are central to the educational mission. With the successful inauguration of the N1 billion Centre, OkoPoly joined the league of other institutions across the globe, which have embraced information and communication technology (ICT), as a basic tool that drives economic growth, national competitiveness and social transformation. According to the Rector of the institution, Dr Chioma Awuzie, the future belongs to those institutions that can equip their students and young people with the skills to create, innovate and compete globally. “And that is why the Federal Polytechnic Oko is positioning itself to be at the forefront of Nigeria’s digital transformation agenda,” she added. She noted that as the rector, she has placed digital transformation, innovation, skills development and technology-driven enterprise within the institution’s strategic direction by increasingly moving the traditional classroom towards a productive and active environment. She argued that the polytechnic of the future must go beyond awarding certificates to preparing students to thrive in a rapidly changing world. She said her leadership has embraced strategic interventions and partnerships capable of transforming the polytechnic into a dynamic ecosystem, where technology meets education, skills meet opportunity, innovation meets enterprise and ideas are transformed into impact. “One of the most significant manifestations of this vision is the polytechnic’s emergence as the South-East hub of the ICT Experience Centre under the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Initiative, sponsored by the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund), recently commissioned by Her Excellency, Sen. Remi Tinubu in Anambra,” she stated. In his remarks, the Chairman of the TETFund Board of Trustees, Aminu Bello Masari, disclosed that OkoPoly was one of the six institutions selected nationwide as pioneer beneficiaries of the project. He explained that the centres were approved under TETFund’s 2024 intervention activities and implemented across the six geopolitical zones at a total cost of N1 billion per zone. He said the intervention recognises the increasing importance of technology to education and national development while supporting programmes under the Renewed Hope Initiative, describing the centre as an enduring platform for translating the First Lady’s vision for youth empowerment into tangible opportunities. Also in his remarks, TETFund Executive Secretary, Sonny Echono said that the project represents an investment in human capital and the future of Nigerian youths. He said it was consistent with TETFund’s commitment to developing Nigeria’s human capital and promoting a knowledge-driven economy. Echono thanked President Bola Tinubu for providing a policy environment conducive to people-centred interventions and commended the First Lady for her commitment to women empowerment and youth development. In her address, Dr Awuzie also described the project as a landmark achievement for the institution, adding that it would provide students and lecturers with practical exposure to Artificial Intelligence, cybersecurity, robotics, software development and other emerging technologies. She said the N1 billion Centre represents a practical expression of the First Lady’s vision that young people must be given tools, opportunities and an enabling environment to discover their talents, acquire relevant skills and become productive contributors to national development. She expressed gratitude to TETFund for its continued intervention at the Federal Polytechnic, Oko, and further appealed to the First Lady and other stakeholders for urgent intervention to address challenges confronting the polytechnic, particularly the threatening erosion in parts of its environment, support towards provision of adequate perimeter fencing for the three campuses and rehabilitation of internal road network in the institution. She said the Centre is majorly powered by solar system to ensure regular power supply. She also said the Polytechnic would partner professional ICT consultants for sustainability of the project, hoping that it would impact more on the entire South Eastern youths Also inaugurated were an ultra-modern chemical engineering department and a digital examination centre for students, among others. For OkoPoly, the event was also an opportunity to showcase the developmental strides of Awuzie’s administration such as the completion of TETFund sponsored building, completion and furnishing of skills acquisition centre, revival of the Polytechnic’s water factory and bakery, among others. She has also taken issues of staff and students’ welfare, discipline, academic reinvention and programme development, anti-cultism, financial transparency, infrastructure and stronger stakeholder relationships to another level since assumption of duty about two years ago. The highlights of the event included conferring an award of performance on the Rector by the National Board for Technical Education (NBTE). Okoye wrote in from Lagos. The post Day First Lady commissioned ICT hub at Oko Polytechnic appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: God remembers in the ember months, by Funmi Komolafe
items.description: Gradually, we are coming to the end of the year, my prayer is that the LORD keeps us beyond this year and gives us the grace to end the year joyfully in Jesus name. Brethren, the reality is that we have only a few months to go in 2026. The past eight months have been quite eventful. In these Ember months, do you still find yourself helpless concerning a particular issue? You may be helpless because you are limited as a human being but there is GOD that is the helper of the helpless. That God is available to attend to your needs. Your relationship with Him should give you hope even when everything around you seems to be contrary to your expectation. The last thing a Christian should do is give up on himself or herself. When you do that, your Christian credentials becomes questionable. It means that your faith is at the peripheral level. It isn’t deep enough to trust the LORD. Apostle Paul and his friend had an experience of helplessness while travelling in a ship. Acts 27 vs. 18-20 (NIV) tells the story. “ We took such a violent battering from the storm that the next day they began to throw the cargo overboard. On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands. When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the storm continued raging, we finally gave up all hope of being saved.” This according to the Bible happened to them because they failed to listen to the pieces of advice given to them by Apostle Paul. When they lost hope of survival, Apostle Paul said to them in verses 21 -24: “ …. Men you should have taken my advice not to sail from Crete; then you would have spared yourselves this damage and loss. But I urge you to keep up your courage, because not one of you will be lost; only the ship will be destroyed. Last night an angel of the God whose I am and whom I serve stood beside me and said, Do not be afraid, Paul. You must stand trial before Caesar; and God has graciously given you the lives of all who sail with you. So keep your courage, men, for I have faith in God that it will happen just as he told me”. Brethren, Paul’s friends took the wrong advice and got into trouble. They became helpless and almost perished but the merciful God remembered them and gave hope that they would not perish. I may not know what challenge you are passing through but in your own interest, do not give up. When you give up on God, you give in to the devil and you may never testify. With the ember months, you may be saying to yourself, this year is gone again and I am not married let alone think of being a mother or a father. Or are you saying, promotion has again eluded me this year? Perhaps what is important to you is starting a new project but nothing seems to be happening. For someone else it could be would I survive this health challenge? These and other similar circumstances could make one helpless but one can still be hopeful even in the state of helplessness. 1st Peter 5 vs. 5 and 6 tells us: “ Humble yourselves, therefore, under God’s mighty hand, that he may lift you up in due time. Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you”. Brethren, to receive a miracle you first need to humble yourself with total submission to God and obedience to his commands. Simply put, keep sins out of your life and establish a relationship with God. God created every one of us but it is not all of us that have a relationship with Him. Most of us turn to God when we find ourselves helpless but that isn’t the way to go. Even when you have achieved, you still need to give glory to God that made it possible. Once you become helpless, a situation where no one can help you and you cannot help yourself, you need to place you worries before the LORD JESUS. The Bibles tells us “ he cares for you”. Since he cares for you, you need to find out what his word says about that situation, and then you begin to call on him to step into the situation for you. When we pray along this line, we are simply saying, “ O God remember me”. Job 8 vs. 5-7: “ But if you will look to God and plead with the Almighty, if you are pure and upright, even now he will rouse himself on your behalf and restore you to your rightful place. Your beginnings will seem humble, so prosperous will your future be”. In other words, those issues that are your worries now, would soon become issues that you would have to celebrate. The ember months are the months that many people give up but Beloved, the ember months are the months that God remembers anyone that has been crying to him for help. Whatever it is, brethren, keep hope alive. Beloved, when you seem helpless, many would mock you but if you have hope in the LORD that would give you strength to overcome mockers. During the September Holy Ghost night, Pastor Jide Akiode an assistant general overseer, while preaching, told the story of how he has been dedicating babies of members but he didn’t have a child. This challenge didn’t stop him from serving the LORD. He served like Zachariah and God came forth for him. Pastor Akiode told the story of how he was on a mission assignment and a lady that hosted him and others asked him what clothes she should buy for his children. According to him, “ as at that time I had no children”. The man that was considered barren told him to get the clothes for a boy and a girl. He said, he received the gift and showed it to his wife when he returned home. “We kept it somewhere. Those things, when our children arrived, they used it. The Pastor said he was called barren for 19 years and four months. He received the clothes because he remained hopeful with the word of the Lord in Deuteronomy 7 vs. 14 ( KJV) : “ Thou shalt be blessed above all people: there shall not be male or female barren among you, or among your cattle”. Since he remained hopeful God visited him with a set of twins. A boy and a girl. If the Pastor had told the person that gave him a gift to buy clothes for a boy or a girl only, that is most likely what God would have given him but he asked with faith for two and God gave him a set of twins. Beloved when it seems hope is lost that is when the God of wonders steps into a situation. Be hopeful, God will remember you these ember months in Jesus name. The post God remembers in the ember months, by Funmi Komolafe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ortom and his 23 cars’ ‘bonus’, by Dele Sobowale
items.description: “As I talk to you, after I left office, vehicles that were given to me legitimately by government, this government went and seized them in a manner that was not befitting” – Former Governor Samuel Ortom of Benue State Last week, former Governor Donald Duke of Cross River declared that military rule was, in many respects, better than civil rule since 1999. I cannot agree more. I had the privilege of visiting about seven former military governors before 1999. No military governor had up to 23 cars assigned to the Governor’s Office or residence. By contrast, since 1999, a civilian governor with only 23 cars in the office alone would be regarded as extremely prudent. Many have 50 or more. Ortom’s 23 cars have triggered a dispute. Governors, on their way out of office, routinely take what they deem as their entitlements and thus render their states poorer than they met them. Most commentaries on the Ortom’s 23 cars have been superficial. The impression they have created is that only 23 cars were taken away. Nothing can be further from the truth. Ortom was not the only beneficiary of that largesse. It is quite possible that over 100 cars were taken away as parting gifts – with Ortom’s approval – as I will explain shortly. Ortom revealed the hidden truth by saying, with a straight face, that the vehicles were allocated to him and other members of his administration through the State Executive Council, SEC, after they had been used for more than four years. It was the worst defence for an assault on public funds ever uttered by a former official. It provided a window into the minds of top government officials everywhere – irrespective of political party affiliation. Every State Executive Council, SEC, comprises of the governor, the deputy governor, the Secretary to the State Government and commissioners. All the others are selected or appointed by the governor, and, with the exception of the deputy governor, can be removed from office. In other words, the SEC is created by the governor and can take no independent decision of its own. It is not an autonomous body. Stripped of the subterfuge surrounding it, the decision to allocate 23 cars to Ortom amounted to the governor deciding to go home with the cars and getting his echoes in SEC to endorse it. Ortom, inadvertently, disclosed that more cars than 23 were driven home by his government officials when he claimed that the SEC allocated the vehicles in dispute to him “and other members of his administration”. Since “the other members of his administration start with the SEC, it stands to reason that the deputy governor, the Secretary to State Government, all the commissioners, the Chief of Staff, several Special Advisers, heads of state agencies etc, were also allowed to go home with cars declared over four years old – even if by one day. Nobody has documented the number of cars Ortom and “the other members of his administration” took away. Over 100 vehicles might be involved. That leads to the next question because it strikes at the heart of why poverty is increasing in Nigeria. IS A CAR FOUR YEARS OLD READY FOR THE JUNKYARD? Most Nigerians known to me, including those driving corporate official cars, are driving vehicles more than five years old. Mine is 12 years old; and can still break the speed limit anywhere in the world. I also own a LAGRIDE Taxi, now four years old. The Chinese made car was offered four years ago at N4.8 million; down payment N1.82 million and balance to be paid in installments. Today, the car costs N25 million new; and offers have been made to buy my used one for N11-13 million. Obviously, when any government gives away, at far less than market value, to departing officials, the public loses. Ortom’s 23 cars, as well as the others allocated to members of his administration, would have fetched almost five times whatever they paid for them. To put the matter in perspective, Benue State would have to pay nothing less than N6 trillion just to replace the vehicles. Left untouched is the question: What else was taken away – furniture, generators, air-conditioners, borehole pumps? Outgoing officials are never satisfied with taking cars with them. “Laws grind the poor, and rich [as well as powerful] men rule the law” – Oliver Goldsmith, 1728-1774 The other half of his self-defence concerns the legality of the allocations. That the law is an ass has been well-established; so is the fact that what we often call law might be injustice codified. Strictly speaking, everything Abacha did was supported by laws passed as decrees. Justice was never considered. Civilian governments also make laws which are inherently unjust to the masses. The regulation allowing some public servants, appointed by the governor, to take away very useful public properties cannot be regarded as equitable given the fact that those who served for 30 or 35 years cannot take away a single pin without being prosecuted. What exactly does an out-going governor want to do with 23 cars? Open a used cars shop? MEANWHILE, GOVERNOR ALIA SETS BACK DEMOCRACY IN BENUE Governor Hyacinth Alia, Catholic cleric, honourably, fought for justice by having the 23 cars taken away by Ortom retrieved. It is not clear whether other cars allocated by Ortom’s SEC members were also seized. If not, the measure would appear personal and discriminatory. It would appear to be partial justice and tainted with vendetta. Frequently, individuals transiently invested with near-absolute power, like Nigerian governors, cross the thin line between the divine and the ridiculous within a short time. When Alia, for the second time, blocked Peter Obi from moving freely about in Benue State, he betrayed democracy and the Constitution of Nigeria he swore to uphold. He failed the democracy test. He even failed the test of advanced education. His tenure is limited by the Constitution. Obviously, he will become an ex-governor one day – without armed escorts to protect him and clear the way. He has established a precedent; which will make it legitimate for any governor in Nigeria to block his right of passage. Two examples in Nigerian history should serve as warning to Alia. Military Head of State, Obasanjo, passed the decree under which General Gowon would have been executed in 1976 – if Britain had not granted the deposed leader political asylum. The same decree, with slight amendment, was used by Abacha to nail his former boss. He was saved by divine intervention. Malam El-Rufai, as governor of Kaduna State, had critics, living in other states, arrested, brought to Kaduna State and detained without bail for days – before media protests got them released on bail. Today, El-Rufai is in detention by the DSS and ICPC, without bail for almost six months. The same media, held in contempt by El-Rufai, has now undertaken the campaign to get him released. As one of our founding fathers, Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, reminded us before passing to eternal life: “No condition is permanent” Governor Alia should climb down from his high horse and apologise to Obi and Nigerians. FROM SAD SAM TO UNCLE SAM: BIOGRAPHY OF A LEGEND “A well-written life is as rare as a well-spent one” – Thomas Carlyle, 1795-1881. Uncle Sam’s life is a splendidly lived life. It has not been as well-written as I would have wanted for reasons too many to explain now. Time was my principal antagonist. From the time the idea of the book was conceived till the books rolled off the press, I had only seven and a half months. That was uncharacteristic haste. ATTAH: ARCHITECT OF A NEW DEMOCRATIC DAWN took 13 years; VANGUARD BOOK OF QUOTATIONS lasted 34 years. The difference is clear. Uncle Sam has never wanted his biography written while alive. At least six people would have done it before me. I was also under that restriction for years. I was prepared to wait to write a post-humous book – until 2020; when cancer almost took my life. It was during COVID-19. Yet, Uncle Sam visited me every morning and evening during my five months in hospital. In my darkest moment in life, he provided the hope and reason for survival. Unknown to him and everybody else, I almost died before him Obviously, I could go before him without expressing appreciation; or he could go without ever knowing how deeply grateful I am. Two unacceptable options. As his 90th birthday approached, the inspiration came from somebody else; who was just as concerned that Uncle Sam might leave the world without anybody to let him know how several of us feel about him. It was risky assignment; with very little time to do it. Only someone with one foot in the grave, like me, could dare to do it. I just hope Uncle Sam understands. It will not be launched; in obedience to Uncle Sam’s wishes. Direct sales only. Kindly order your copy by calling. Thank you. Follow me on Facebook @ J Israel Biola The post Ortom and his 23 cars’ ‘bonus’, by Dele Sobowale appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Why men ought to be more concerned about their health!
items.description: By Bunmi Sofola Looks as if Nigerian men are paying the price for neglecting their health, with more men dying prematurely every year. But common male health problems can be detected and treated earlier (if not prevented) with better awareness and regular check-ups. Listed are some of the health issues highlighted by experts and how to cope with them. A Testicular Lump: Testicular cancer is the most common cancer in men aged 20 to 35, so any lumps or abnormalities in testicles should have urgent medical attention. Most lumps are benign but it is vital to get them checked because treatment is much more effective if cancer is diagnosed early. Go to: www.orchid-cancer.org.uk. Abdominal Obesity: This affects 30 per cent of adult men. Fat around the midriff is particularly dangerous because it secrets toxins that increase the risk of various medical disorders. Those affected are made more susceptible to high cholesterol, diabetes, hypertension and cardiovascular disease. Abdominal obesity can also lead to fat-related cancers such as bowel and pancreatic cancer. Go to: www.nationalobesityforum.org.uk. An Enlarged Prostate: This presses on the tube that carries urine from the bladder, making it harder to pass urine. This can be a sign of several prostate diseases, including cancer. Other symptoms include frequently waking up in the night to pass urine and a pain or burning when you do so. Go to: www.orchidcancer.org.uk. Impotence: Most men have problems getting or keeping an erection at some point in their life, but if the condition lasts for several weeks, a doctor’s advice should be sought. Erectile dysfunction can be a sign of more serious conditions, such as heart disease, diabetes or high blood pressure. Lifestyle changes can help, though medication such as sildenafil (Viagra) might be prescribed. Go to: www.nhs.uk/conditions/erectile-dysfunction. Strokes: Strokes are the most common cause of death. Although there’s a genetic predisposition, an unhealthy lifestyle more than doubles your stroke risk, according to researchers at the University of East Anglia. They stated that even slightest raised blood pressure can dramatically raise the threat of stroke among younger and middle-aged people, so be sure to go for regular checkups. Self-help: Key changes in lifestyle can play a huge part in warding off this common killer. Choose a breakfast cereal fortified in folic acid to raise levels of foliate, a B vitamin that is thought to reduce the risk of stroke. Other good sources of foliate are brown rice, Brussels sprouts, asparagus and oranges. See your dentist regularly, as gum disease is linked to stroke and heart disease risk. A study of 100,000 people found that those who had their teeth scraped and polished at least once a year had a 24 per cent lower risk of a heart attack and a 13 per cent lower risk of a stroke in the seven years following. It is thought that when the gum becomes inflamed, bacteria leaks into the bloodstream and causes damage in the blood vessels. Go to: www.stroke.orR.uk. Type 2 Diabetes: The main symptoms are: needing to pass urine more than usual, especially at night, feeling thirsty; losing weight without trying to; tiredness; blurred eyesight; genital itching or thrush; and cuts that take a long time to heal. Self-help: “Up to 80 per cent of cases can be delayed or prevented with lifestyle changes,” says Pav Kalsi, clinical adviser at Diabetes UK. Try the following measures:- Watch your waistline: “Even if you have a normal body mass index (BMI), a large waist – defined as 31.5in or more for women and 35in or more for men – means you’re most at risk,’ warns Pav Kalsi. Eat more fibre: Walnuts and whole-grain foods such as brown rice and wholemeal bread and pasta are said to help. Reduce Stress: Researcher at the University College London claim that having a stressful job can double your risk of diabetes. If you’re overdoing it, make sure you set aside at least two nights a week for quality relation time. Go to: Use the online assessment tool at Diabetes UK (www.diabetes.org.uk/riskscore) to measure your risk. Moles: Check moles regularly for changes in colour or shape. Most changes are harmless but see your doctor if a mole has altered in appearance, becomes itchy or if it starts bleeding. It can then be checked and removed if necessary. The post Why men ought to be more concerned about their health! appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ELECTIONS: Nigeria is still pursuing shadows, by Tonnie Iredia
items.description: In less than 4 months from now, Nigeria will hold its 2027 general elections; yet, not many would believe the assurances by the electoral body that the process will be free and fair. No one can blame the doubting Thomases because the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC is notorious for not keeping its word. Just before the last general elections in 2023, INEC told the nation that it would premise its operations on modern technology: indicating specifically that there would be both manual and electronic collation of votes etc. But it neither kept the promise nor did it present a posture of an organization that meant what it previously promised. It did not even convey any iota of remorse for misleading people. If therefore some people have continued to reject the results of many segments of the election, it is not because such persons are bad losers, instead it is because our elections are intrinsically incredible. It is simplistic to argue that after the highest court of the land has determined a case, it should be rested. However, to abide by a verdict of the Supreme Court because one believes in the rule of law does not mean that every such case was persuasive or seen by everyone as real justice. For example, there is a particular governorship election where our apex court had ruled that the correct candidate of the winning party was candidate A. On its part, INEC eventually declared candidate B as the winner. But our courts disagreed, recounted the votes and gave victory to candidate C. The case was further compounded by the fact that in the end, the recount turned out to have more votes than voters. Here, there are several posers. To start with, how was candidate C able to contest an election that the court had earlier recognized candidate A as the lawful contestant of the same party? Again, why did the same court accept to recount the votes at the instance of candidate C? Answers to these questions would establish clearly that credible elections are different from those for which people work to the answer while leaving substance to pursue shadows. If we want to stop pursuing shadows, the first thing is for INEC to do something about politicians within its fold. As referees, all persons within INEC are by our constitution not allowed to be partisan. They must therefore be above board like Caeser’s wife. Consequently, at the point of nomination of National and Resident Electoral Commissioners, INEC must do all in its powers to draw the attention of all relevant authorities to the grave adverse implications of allowing anyone known to be a card carry member of a political party to be appointed as a member of INEC. In the case of staff, there is the story that some of them who are in certain technical and strategic areas are often elevated to commissionership at the instance of governors of their states to get them deployed to cover nefarious activities. In other words, INEC knows the culprits and as such should not be pursuing shadows having colluded with those politicising the commission When the military was planning to quit the political scene many years ago, it was imagined that there was the need for a transition programme because military rule had been prolonged beyond public expectation. The nation settled for guided democracy where the electoral body was mandated to supervise the new political parties. President Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida during his tenure set up two parties, appointed civil servants to administer them and at a point asked the electoral commission to draft constitutions for the parties. It was as if our political parties were destined not to grow. Although democracy was restored in 1999, we seem to have continued with the idea of supervising our political parties some 27 years after. When will our parties come of age or is it a case of transition without end? This question may have to be answered in the positive if no effort is made to let INEC serve as referee only without in addition serving as coach. Our parties must be allowed to determine who their flag bearers are in line with the spirit of the decision of the supreme court. There is no need for a continuation of the power given to the electoral body to monitor events such as party primaries. The clear evidence that the power is superfluous is reflected in the fact that the law also says INEC may choose to monitor or not to monitor the same events thereby creating an obvious ambivalence that invigorates shadow chasers. The National Assembly is an integral part of the shadow-chasing team because each time a general election is due, our legislators produce another Electoral Act that is never directed at solving the real issue at stake. In view of the convoluted nature of our electoral system, no voter believes that his vote will count in an election. Rather than providing for electronic transmission of results which is internationally recognized as the best practice and which can generally assuage the fears of the people, our law makers waste energies on semantics which at the end of the day, produces an amendment that takes nothing away from statusquo. Is it not strange that at the end of each election, more people are dissatisfied with the latest edition of our Electoral Act? Does it not amount to shadow-chasing if we constantly amend the Electoral Act without achieving any purpose? The situation is the same with the general impression that is given in our clime that nothing else apart from elections is important to Nigeria. As a result, we usually close all other businesses on voting day. But in reality, there is nothing special about how we manage the conduct of elections which these days features open vote buying and other forms of electoral malpractices. Quite often, the electoral commission is left in panic when a court decides that a political party should be added to the list of contestants on the eve of voting, well after INEC had concluded the printing of materials for the elections. While it is in line with the rule of law to obey court orders, the latter ought not to be done to destabilize society. Apart from the fact that the decision involves additional expenses and disrupts otherwise concluded logistic arrangements, it also puts a contestant in a disadvantaged position. Here, it is easy to recall the 10-year-old case of candidate Eyitayo Jegede whose participation in the governorship election in Ondo state was not decided by the judiciary until some 48 hours before voting day leaving him with only 24hours for campaigns. The idea of litigation ‘without end’ from beginning till voting day is obviously unwise and except the trend is redressed, free and fair elections in Nigeria may remain a mirage. There is therefore no better time than now for a deadline to be fixed for the determination of preelection cases in the country. Is it not hypocrisy that we are ready to allow the litigation of pre-election matters till the day of voting but unwilling to set up an election tribunal to deal with election offences? Could it be that those who are to set up the framework for dealing with election offences are the patrons of the wrongdoers? The issue of polling agents also deserves some comments here. Bearing in mind that the law allows all political parties to have agents to represent their interests at different polling centres, many people have often asked political parties who fail to nominate agents to hold themselves accountable for any negative happenings at locations where they are not represented by agents. I am however unable to agree with this because the absence of polling agents of some political parties during elections cannot change a credible election to a bad one. After all, it is not the duty of the agents to officiate during elections. They are merely to take note of any event, omission, error or malpractice to enable their parties to appropriately ventilate their grievances where necessary. Let’s not forget that there are thousands of poll officials recruited by INEC and remunerated from tax payers’ money to assist the commission to do its job. Such officials are not there to favour any political party; instead, they are appointed to ensure a credible process on behalf of all. What this suggests therefore is that with or without party agents, an election should be free, fair and credible. The presence of party agents is essentially to make assurance doubly sure. Nigeria can have a successful election if what she pursues is the substance and not the shadows of elections. items.title: Survol de drones au Luxembourg : Une enquête lancée avec l'appui de l'OTAN
items.description: Les autorités luxembourgeoises enquêtent après la détection de drones ayant entraîné la suspension temporaire du trafic au principal aéroport du pays dans la nuit, a déclaré samedi le Premier ministre Luc Frieden. M. Frieden a indiqué que le Luxembourg coopère avec ses alliés de l'Otan au sujet de cet incident, qui survient dans un contexte de vives inquiétudes en Europe concernant des attaques hybrides en provenance de Russie. Il a précisé que la présence de « drones potentiellement plus grands » dans l'espace aérien du pays avait été observée « ces derniers jours » , mais qu'il était trop tôt pour se prononcer sur leur provenance. « Nous sommes en train d'analyser la situation » , a déclaré le Premier ministre lors d'une conférence de presse télévisée. Le trafic a été brièvement interrompu à l'aéroport de Luxembourg dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi après la détection de drones qui effectuaient un vol non autorisé dans le périmètre. Les opérations de vol à l'aéroport de Luxembourg ont ensuite repris. Cette suspension constituait « une mesure de précaution pour assurer la sécurité des passagers, des équipages des compagnies aériennes, du personnel de l'aéroport et des appareils » , a expliqué l'aéroport. La compagnie nationale Luxair a indiqué que plus de 1.800 passagers avaient été impactés par cette suspension, qui a entraîné la déroutement de 17 vols à l'arrivée vers d'autres aéroports tels que Bruxelles, Paris et Francfort. « Luxair travaille en étroite collaboration avec Lux-Airport, les autorités compétentes et ses partenaires (…) pour assister les passagers concernés et rétablir son programme de vols » , a déclaré la compagnie aérienne. Les opérations ont repris samedi, mais d'autres perturbations et effets en cascade étaient attendus, a-t-elle ajouté. « C'est nouveau pour le Luxembourg, mais ce n'est pas complètement nouveau pour nos pays voisins » , a ajouté M. Frieden à propos des observations de drones, à l'issue d'une réunion d’urgence avec les ministres luxembourgeois de la Défense et de l'Intérieur. Depuis la guerre entre l'Ukraine et la Russie en 2022, les alliés européens de Kiev ont tiré la sonnette d'alarme concernant des « attaques hybrides » attribuées à la Russie. Ces attaques englobent des survols de drones près de sites sensibles, des violations de l'espace aérien et des cyberattaques, selon eux. Les incursions de drones ont principalement touché des pays situés sur le flanc oriental de l'Otan. Mais des aéronefs sans pilote non autorisés ont également été repérés survolant des sites sensibles en Belgique et au Danemark l'an dernier. Et cette année, un drone chargé d'explosifs a été découvert dans un aéroport allemand, Berlin mettant en cause Moscou. « Nous veillerons, avec nos partenaires, à pouvoir garantir la sécurité de nos populations », a souligné M.Frieden. items.title: Avant son envol, Damaro livre sa première réaction : « je reviens en début novembre »
items.description: L’ancien président de l’Assemblée nationale, Amadou Damaro Camara, a réagi avant son départ de la Guinée pour l’étranger, où il doit poursuivre sa prise en charge médicale. Dans ses premiers mots avant son envol, l’ancien responsable politique a notamment exprimé sa reconnaissance aux autorités pour l’autorisation de sortie du territoire ainsi que pour l’accompagnement dont il dit avoir bénéficié. Autorisé à quitter le pays pour des soins médicaux spécialisés, Amadou Damaro Camara a tenu à livrer sa première réaction avant son départ. Il a insisté sur la nécessité de préserver l’intérêt national, tout en saluant la décision des autorités de lui permettre de poursuivre ses soins à l’étranger. « Le pays est au-dessus de chacun des Guinéens. Il y a toujours la nécessité de faire un effort pour faire avancer le pays. La Guinée est notre bien commun, nous devons la préserver. Je vais aller me soigner, faire au moins une visite… pas une visite plus sélective, mais plus spécialisée, et je reviens en début novembre. […] C'est une révélation… On me laisse partir me soigner, mais on m'a assisté pour mes besoins. Pour cela, je remercie les autorités » , a-t-il déclaré. Amadou Damaro Camara doit ainsi bénéficier d’une prise en charge médicale spécialisée à l’étranger. Son départ intervient dans un contexte particulier, l’ancien président de l’Assemblée nationale fait partie des grandes figures de l’ancien régime dont la situation judiciaire et politique fait l’objet d’une attention particulière. Dans le même temps, l’ancien Premier ministre Dr Ibrahima Kassory Fofana a également été autorisé à quitter la Guinée pour poursuivre ses soins à l’étranger. Pour son déplacement, un vol spécial a été affrété par le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya. Ces départs pour raisons médicales marquent une nouvelle évolution dans la situation des deux anciens hauts responsables, alors que leur séjour à l’étranger doit désormais leur permettre de poursuivre leurs prises en charge médicales.

items.title: Le ministre de la Culture appelle à l’élargissement du festival du Trarza et à en faire un rendez-vous national
items.description: Le ministre de la Culture, des Arts, de la Communication et des Relations avec le Parlement, porte-parole du gouvernement, El-Houssein Ould Medou, a appelé vendredi à développer le festival du patrimoine du Trarza, à élargir la participation s’y afférent et à diversifier ses programmes, afin qu’il devienne un rendez-vous national permettant de faire connaître le patrimoine de la région ainsi que son potentiel culturel, économique et touristique. Lors de l’inauguration de la deuxième édition du festival à Tiguint, Ould Medou a déclaré que le patrimoine représentait la mémoire de la société et son capital culturel, soulignant que sa mise en valeur ne signifiait pas vivre dans le passé, mais s’inspirer de ses valeurs pour construire le présent et envisager l’avenir. Il a ajouté que la documentation du patrimoine et sa mise en valeur par des moyens modernes permettent de le transformer en savoir, en produits culturels et en opportunités d’emploi, de création et d’investissement, en particulier pour les jeunes. Il a souligné que la préservation du patrimoine s’inscrit dans une vision nationale visant à faire de la culture et des arts un moteur du développement et à renforcer l’unité nationale, insistant sur l’importance d’impliquer les jeunes et de transformer l’héritage en contenu culturel, en produits artistiques et touristiques, ainsi qu’en opportunités économiques. Les activités du festival se déroulent sur trois jours et comprennent des spectacles, des tables rondes et des conférences sur le patrimoine culturel, scientifique, artistique et social de la région du Trarza.

items.title: Trump says he plans to form AI Force, appoint AI 'Czar'
items.description: US President Donald Trump said Saturday that he is forming an "AI Force" and will announce an "AI Czar" in the near future. In a post on his Truth Social account, Trump said he would not stand by and let the "decimation or destruction" of AI happen. "We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry. Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows! However, we will also be looking for BAD, and we can do that, very easily, with our already existing Criminal and Civil Justice System," Trump said. Trump also described AI as the next Industrial Revolution or Internet, and said it could possibly account for as much as 25% of US gross domestic product. Trump did not provide details on the structure of the planned "AI Force" or the role of the "AI Czar." The announcement comes amid growing debate in the United States over the rapid development of AI and its potential risks.

items.title: Govt finalises sweeping civil service reforms
items.description: • 11 specialised professional cadres in bureaucracy proposed • BS-20, above posts may be opened to officials, academics, private-sector professionals ISLAMABAD: Amid concerns over declining standards and lack of specialisation in the bureaucracy, the federal government has finalised a sweeping restructuring of the civil service, proposing 11 new professional cadres, a complete overhaul of the Central Superior Services (CSS) examination and senior-level promotions and linking officials’ performance to financial rewards. The proposed reforms, estimated to cost Rs11 billion to implement, seek to reshape recruitment, training, career progression, performance evaluation and the institutional structure of the federal bureaucracy. The package was unveiled at a consultative session on civil service reforms chaired by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal on Saturday. The session was attended by Senator Saleem Mandviwalla, Federal Minister Aleem Khan, former PTI federal minister Asad Umar, senior policymakers, sector specialists and other stakeholders. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had constituted two committees on civil service reforms, which have held 18 meetings since September 2024 and reached consensus on 43 of 46 recommendations. The proposed new professional cadres include HR, Law, Engine­ering, Science and Technology, IT and Telecom, Energy, Climate, Agriculture and Forestry, Education and Health groups. The Establishment Division wou­ld be converted into a Human Reso­urce and Organisation Development Division, while federal decision-making would be reduced from five tiers to three. Under the proposed National Executive Service (NES) structure, posts in BS-20 and above would be filled through open competition on five-year contracts against published performance targets, with serving officers, private-sector professionals and academics competing on equal terms. The Police Service and Foreign Service would remain outside the NES. It also proposes piloting performance-linked pay in the federal secretariat and a retirement package comprising a Rs5 million lump sum funded through monthly deductions, along with subsidised health insurance. The new policy also draws on Pakistan Army human resource practices, proposing replacement of the one-day viva voce with a multi-day competency-based assessment on the pattern of ISSB. The model emphasises psychometric, emotional intelligence and leadership assessments at recruitment, placement on the principle of the “right person for the right job”, specialised training and multi-tier performance evaluation. It also draws on the army’s structured promotion system, under which progression becomes increasingly selective at senior ranks and promotion decisions are made collectively by boards on prescribed criteria rather than individual discretion. A key shift under the proposed system is recruitment according to specialisation, ending the existing arrangement under which officers can be allocated to fields they have never studied. The CSS examination itself would not be abolished. Candidates would have the option of attempting five compulsory papers — Essay, Précis and Composition, Islamiat, Pakistan Studies and Current Affairs — in Urdu, while functional proficiency in English would remain a screening requirement. The preliminary test threshold would be raised from 33pc to 40pc, with analytical reasoning added and negative marking removed. The package also proposes published assessment criteria, full digitisation and reduction of the recruitment cycle to six months or less, alongside affirmative measures to fill unfilled quota seats for Balochistan, Sindh, minorities and women. The performance system would also be recast, with every ministry entering into an annual performance agreement with the prime minister and individual targets flowing from it. Officials would be evaluated twice a year, while 5pc of employee-related expenditure would be earmarked for performance-based honoraria. The National Management Course would be shortened from 18 weeks to 10, while existing national and specialised training institutions would be merged into a National University of Public Administration. No constitutional amendment would be required for the package. Following approval, an implementation committee would oversee execution, report monthly to the prime minister and target full implementation within 120 days. Published in Dawn, September 20th, 2026

items.title: ‘GB peaks more valuable than oil reservoirs’
items.description: Reinhold Messner and his wife, Diane, climb a rock to view Nanga Parbat, remembering when he and his late brother, Gunther, climbed that same rock in 1970 before their historic expedition.—Photo by the writer • Renowned climber Messner warns ‘white mountains’ may not survive another decade; calls for urgent action • Celebrates 82nd birthday in Islamabad • Reflects on his lifelong bond with Pakistan ISLAMABAD: Renowned Italian mountaineer Reinhold Messner warned that rapid glacial melting threatens the survival of Pakistan’s peaks, declaring the high mountains of Gilgit-Baltistan “more valuable than oil reservoirs in Arab countries”. Expressing deep concern for the changing environment, the alpinist said some “white mountains” in the region may only survive another 10 to 15 years without better environmental management, pledging that he and his team remain determined to help save the remaining ice. The 82-year-old issued the warning while celebrating his birthday during a 12-day visit to the mountain areas of GB with his wife, Diane. The trip, which ran from Sept 6 to Sept 16, culminated in a birthday celebration organised by Nanga Parbat Adventure Pakistan at the Serena Hotel in Islamabad. Italian Ambassador to Pak­istan Ugo Ciarlatani, German Ambassador Ina Lepel and prominent Pakistani mountaineers, including Nazir Sabir and Liver Khan, attended the ceremony to honour Messner’s historic achievements. Beyond his climbing legacy, Mr Messner continues to give back to the region. Mr Khan, a long-time friend, highlighted Messner’s ongoing connection to the local communities that aided him during his perilous descent of Nanga Parbat over 50 years ago. Over the decades, Mr Messner has helped establish several schools in the Diamer valleys, including one named in memory of his younger brother, Mr Gunther. “I look forward to … the schools, places where the future is written, where hope grows stronger than loss,” Mr Messner noted. The return to Pakistan brought profound sentimental reflections for the man widely regarded as one of history’s greatest high-altitude climbers. Days before his birthday, Mr Messner stopped at a rock situated along the Karakoram Highway near Thalichy, which offers a clear view of Nanga Parbat. He climbed the rock again, just as he did in 1970 when he and Mr Gunther first saw the mountain rising in the distance. For Mr Messner, the region holds both triumph and deep personal tragedy. He and Mr Gunther reached the summit of Nanga Parbat in 1970 via the Rupal Face, but disaster struck during their descent on the Diamir side. Mr Gunther was swept away by an avalanche and died. Mr Messner survived but lost seven toes to severe frostbite. His cla­ims about his brother’s death were vindicated in 2005 when Mr Gunther’s remains were fin­ally discovered on the Diamir Face. Mr Messner was accused by his teammates, including Herrl­igko­ffer, of abandoning his bro­ther solely to gain the bragging rights of traversing Nanga Parbat. In 1978, Mr Messner returned to summit Nanga Parbat completely alone. Climbing without supplementary oxygen or support from teammates, he opened a new route on the right side of the Diamir Face, completing the first solo ascent of an 8,000-metre mountain. “To return to Pakistan is to return to the roots of my own becoming,” Mr Messner wrote in a social media post before his arrival. “Here, at Nanga Parbat, I crossed the mountain and lost my brother Gunther, a wound that has never closed but became part of who I am.” Published in Dawn, September 20th, 2026

items.title: GNFS contains fire outbreak at Teshie Lekma Road near Lekma Hospital
items.description: The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) has brought under control a fire outbreak involving several commercial containers at Ebenezer Junction on the Teshie Lekma Road, near Lekma Hospital. The fire affected containers being used for various commercial activities, with a container operated by a vulcaniser reportedly sustaining significant damage. The GNFS said three fire appliances from the Trade Fair, Kasapreko and National Headquarters Fire Stations were deployed to contain the outbreak. In an update on its official Facebook page, the Service said the fire had been brought under control while salvaging operations were underway. “The fire is currently under control as salvaging is being done to prevent reignition,” the GNFS stated. The incident occurred in the busy commercial area along the Teshie Lekma Road. The GNFS has not yet disclosed the cause of the fire or provided details on the extent of property damaged or lost. Salvage operations are continuing as firefighters work to prevent any possible reignition and ensure the area is safe. Further details are expected as the Fire Service assesses the incident and determines the cause of the outbreak.

items.title: Zondoma : Les acteurs de l’éducation affûtent les armes pour aborder la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027 dans la CEB de Lèba
items.description: Burkina/Zondoma-Education Zondoma : Les acteurs de l’éducation affûtent les armes pour aborder la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027 dans la CEB de Lèba Lèba, 18 sept. 2026 (AIB)- Les acteurs de la Circonscription d’éducation de base (CEB) de Lèba dans la province du Zondoma se sont concertés, le vendredi 18 septembre 2026, afin de préparer l’année scolaire 2026-2027 qui débute officiellement le 1er octobre 2026. Les premiers responsables de la CEB de Lèba, les directeurs d’écoles ainsi que les enseignants titulaires des classes de CM2 se sont retrouvés ce vendredi 18 septembre 2026 à l’école de Lèba « A ». Cette rencontre de rentrée a constitué un cadre d’échanges autour du bilan de l’année scolaire 2025-2026 et des perspectives pour la nouvelle année qui pointe à l’horizon. Les échanges ont notamment permis à l’encadrement de présenter les nouvelles orientations pour l’année scolaire 2026-2027 et de planifier les différentes activités du premier trimestre. Selon la cheffe de la Circonscription d’éducation de base de Lèba, Albertine Sawadogo/Rimzouré, cette première prise de contact vise à permettre aux acteurs de la CEB, d’identifier les difficultés rencontrées au cours de l’année écoulée et de dégager des solutions idoines pour améliorer les résultats scolaires. Elle a de ce fait, félicité l’ensemble de ses collaborateurs pour les résultats obtenus au cours de l’année précédente et les a encouragés à maintenir le cap afin de relever, ensemble, les défis de l’année scolaire qui s’ouvre. La rencontre a également enregistré la présence d’une délégation de la Direction provinciale de l’Éducation préscolaire, primaire et non formelle (DPEPPNF) du Zondoma, conduite par l’inspecteur général Tido Sogoba. Pour l’inspecteur général, l’objectif de la province demeure inchangé : « il est de zéro échec au CEP », a-t-il rappelé tout en rassurant les acteurs de l’éducation de la disponibilité de la direction provinciale à accompagner l’ensemble des CEB de son ressort pour l’atteinte de leurs objectifs. À l’issue de la rencontre, les acteurs de l’éducation de la CEB de Lèba ont pris l'engagement de renforcer la concertation, d'anticiper les difficultés et de conjuguer leurs efforts pour battre le record des 97,24% de taux de succès de 2026. Agence d’Information du Burkina MB/AZ-DNK

items.title: Zondoma : Cinq CSPS de Gourcy dotés de vidoirs pour renforcer l’hygiène, la gestion des déchets et la sécurité des patients
items.description: Burkina/Zondoma-CSPS Zondoma : Cinq CSPS de Gourcy dotés de vidoirs pour renforcer l’hygiène, la gestion des déchets et la sécurité des patients Gourcy, 18 sept. 2026 (AIB) – Cinq formations sanitaires de la commune de Gourcy ont bénéficié de vidoirs réalisés par l’Association monde rural (AMR) en partenariat avec l’International rescue committee (IRC). La remise officielle de ces ouvrages destinés à améliorer la gestion des déchets et liquides issus des soins dans les salles d’accouchement a eu lieu ce vendredi 18 septembre 2026. Les Centres de santé et de promotion sociale (CSPS) de Zindingessé, Tangaye, Kiblo, Minima-Douré et Koundouba sont les bénéficiaires des vidoirs réalisés grâce au concours de l’AMR et de de son partenaire l’IRC. Dans les formations sanitaires, la remise des ouvrages qui s’est déroulée le vendredi 18 septembre 2026 a connu la présence d’un représentant de la mairie de Gourcy Moustapha Ouédraogo, du technicien en hygiène du district sanitaire de Gourcy Christian Kaboré. A en croire les donateurs, ces ouvrages permettront d’évacuer les déchets et liquides issus des soins dans les salles d’accouchement, contribuant ainsi à réduire les risques liés à l’exposition aux déchets et aux liquides biologiques. « La réalisation de ces vidoirs vise à améliorer les conditions de travail des agents de santé. Cela permet également aux accompagnantes des femmes en travail d’éviter la manipulation directe du sang et, par conséquent, de limiter les risques d’infection », a expliqué la représentante de l’IRC Edwige Ouédraogo, qui dans son message a invité les bénéficiaires à assurer une utilisation responsable des installations afin de préserver leur fonctionnalité. Au CSPS de Minima-Douré, l’infirmier chef de poste, Mahamadi Ouédraogo, a salué la réalisation de ces vidoirs qui, pour lui, malgré leur apparente simplicité, répondent à un besoin important dans les salles d’accouchement. « Auparavant, les accompagnantes étaient amenées à manipuler les déchets, avec un risque d’exposition aux agents infectieux. Avec ces ouvrages, cette situation devrait être améliorée », a-t-il indiqué, tout en remerciant les partenaires pour leur accompagnement. A en croire le représentant de l’AMR, Dr Narcis Congo, ces ouvrages d’assainissement d’une valeur estimée à plus de deux millions de francs CFA ont été réalisés dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du projet OP515 intitulé « Santé, droits sexuels et reproductifs, protection et autonomisation socioéconomique des femmes dans le contexte de crise du Nord du Burkina ». En rappel, dans le même registre, le CSPS du village de Lago dans la commune de Gourcy avait bénéficié de la réfection de sa maternité mise en service en août dernier. Agence d’Information du Burkina YN/AK-DNK

items.title: Agou / rentrée scolaire 2026-2027 : Des fournitures scolaires distribuées aux élèves nécessiteux
items.description: Agou-Gadzépé, 19 sept. (ATOP) – Le député Yossah Yawotsè a distribué, lors d’une tournée effectuée les 17 et 18 septembre dans les différents établissements scolaires publics et privés dans la commune Agou 2, des fournitures scolaires aux élèves nécessiteux. Au total 23 établissements ont été visités dont des écoles primaires d’Amoussoukopé, Adzakpa, Lankui, Wudzralè, Wutegblé, Séva, Adamé, Nyidové, Kotokopé, Kpodzahoun, Zoukpé, Nyitoé, Henonoé; les CEG d’Amoussoukopé, Adzakpa, Glekopé, Adamé, Nyitoé ainsi que les lycées d’Adamé et d’Amoussoukopé. L’honorable sensibilise les élèves à s’attacher aux études Dans ces établissements, le député a remis des paquets de cahiers, des stylos, des craies (blancs et couleurs), ainsi que des effaceurs aux élèves nécessiteux identifiés sur place. En dehors de ces kits scolaires, le député a également offert une tonne de ciment aux responsables de l’école primaire publique groupe A d’Amoussoukopé pour la réhabilitation des marches défectueuses de certains bâtiments. Des ardoisines ont été également offertes à l’EPP Woutegble pour noircir les tableaux. Ce geste permettra aux bénéficiaires d’aborder avec confiance et sérénité la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027 et aussi de donner le meilleur d’eux-mêmes. L’honorable a posté avec les élèves de l’EPP Glekopé Pour l’occasion, des difficultés liées au fonctionnement des écoles ont été relevées par les responsables desdits établissements. Ces difficultés sont, entre autres, le manque d’enseignants, d’électricité, d’eau et aussi la réticence de certains élèves à venir à l’école. Il a été aussi remarqué le vol de certains équipements destinés aux usages de l’eau et d’électrification dans certaines écoles. Le député Yossah Yawotsè a sensibilisé les apprenants à être attentif à l’école et à obéir aux enseignants et aux parents. Il a exhorté les filles à se concentrer sur les études et à ne pas se laisser berner par les les hommes. Les responsables des différents établissements ont témoigné leur gratitude au député pour son geste à l’endroit des élèves nécessiteux ce qui, selon eux, traduit son attachement au développement local à travers l’éducation. ATOP/MET/BSM/AR

items.title: Singer Ed Sheeran says Gaza situation 'unjustifiable' following controversy
items.description: Pop star Ed Sheeran said Saturday the situation in Gaza is "unjustifiable," following a wave of criticism that he had failed to back his opening act who was booted from the tour after making pro-Palestinian comments. The singer, who had previously maintained an apolitical stance, broke his silence on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict in his first show since the controversy involving US rapper Macklemore. "What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate," Sheeran said in Philadelphia.

items.title: Kozah/chefferie traditionnelle : Des acteurs outillés pour une bonne gestion des affaires coutumières
items.description: Kara, 19 sept. (ATOP) – Les acteurs impliqués dans le processus de gestion de la chefferie traditionnelle ont été outillés le samedi 19 septembre à Kara sur les textes et procédures régissant la désignation et la reconnaissance des chefs traditionnels au cours d’un atelier de renforcement de leurs capacités. Organisée par le ministère de l’Administration territoriale, de la Gouvernance locale et des Affaires coutumières, la session a réuni les préfets, les maires, les gardiens des us et coutumes, ainsi que les secrétaires généraux des préfectures et des communes de la région de la Kara. L’objectif visé est de permettre à ces différents acteurs de mieux maîtriser le cadre légal et les procédures inhérentes afin de réduire les incompréhensions et les contestations liées à la désignation et à la reconnaissance des chefs traditionnels. Il s’agit de prévenir les conflits et de favoriser une gestion consensuelle de cette institution au sein des communautés. Les travaux ont porté sur trois modules essentiels à savoir les textes législatifs et réglementaires régissant la chefferie traditionnelle ; la composition et le fonctionnement des organes de désignation des chefs traditionnels, ainsi que la composition, l’étude et la transmission des dossiers de reconnaissance des chefs traditionnels. Ouvrant les travaux au nom du ministre de tutelle, le préfet de la Kozah, Col. Bonfo Faré, a rappelé le rôle central de la chefferie traditionnelle dans la société. Garante des us et coutumes, elle contribue a-t-il précisé à la résolution des conflits, au maintien de la cohésion sociale et à la préservation de l’identité culturelle. « Cette entité territoriale constitue également un relais entre l’administration et les populations. La maîtrise du cadre légal et des bonnes pratiques en la matière par chacun de nous est donc un gage indispensable pour une gestion apaisée, transparente et consensuelle de la chefferie traditionnelle », a conclu le représentant du pouvoir central. Le directeur de la Chefferie traditionnelle, Wazabalo Massimlawé a expliqué que ce renforcement de compétences des acteurs impliqués fait suite aux difficultés constatées sur le terrain notamment, la méconnaissance du cadre légal. L’étape de Kara intervient après celles de Dapaong, Mango et Bassar. Les étapes suivantes sont prévues du 21 au 26 septembre prochains respectivement à Sokodé, Atakpamé, Kpalimé, Tsévié et Adétikopé. Le ministère en charge des affaires coutumières envisage également d’autres formations destinées aux chefs traditionnels sur leurs droits, obligations et responsabilités. ATOP/AE/TAL/AR

items.title: Blitta : Des kits scolaires aux meilleurs élèves de l’EPP Touléwayi et du CEG Toulé
items.description: Blitta-Gare, 19 sept. (ATOP) – L’ONG Humanity First Togo-Allemagne a offert, le vendredi 18 septembre au CEG Toulé, des kits scolaires aux 78 meilleurs élèves de l’Ecole primaire publique (EPP) Touléwayi, et du CEG Toulé dans le canton de Tchaloudè (commune Blitta 1). Les kits sont composés de cahiers, d’ardoises, de stylos, de règles, de crayons, de taille crayons, de gommes et de paquets de crayons de couleurs. Ce geste vise à encourager ces apprenants à continuer de bien de travailler et à motiver les autres à faire comme eux. Les bénéficiaires ont été sensibilisés sur la bienfaisance et les gestes humanitaires. Ils ont été conseillés à être des élèves excellents, modèles et à respecter les enseignants ainsi que les parents. Une bénéficiaire reçoit ses fournitures des mains de M. Waseem Outre les articles scolaires pour les élèves studieux, les directions des deux établissements scolaires ont bénéficié des cahiers, des boîtes de craies, d’effaceurs, de stylos, des paquets de crayons de couleurs et des règles. Le missionnaire de l’ONG Humanity First Togo (bureau d’Atakpamé), Waseem Ahmad a souligné que cet appui vient créer l’émulation au sein du monde scolaire pour la quête de l’excellence. Il a précisé que cette activité a été rendue possible grâce au soutien de bonnes volontés, demandant aux bénéficiaires de prier pour ceux-ci pour la poursuite de leurs œuvres caritative. Le directeur du CEG Toulé, Alfa Komi a, au nom des bénéficiaires, remercié le donateur pour le geste humanitaire qui vient soulager les peines des parents en ce début de la rentrée scolaire. Il a promis que les bénéficiaires en feront bon usage pour améliorer leurs résultats scolaires. La cérémonie a connu la présence du représentant du maire de Blitta 1, Méfoirou Séidou, des autorités administratives, politiques, traditionnelles, du corps éducatif, des bénéficiaires et de leurs parents. ATOP/SF/MEK/AR

items.title: Port de Lmhiriz : Bond de 78 % de la valeur des débarquements de la pêche à fin août
items.description: Les débarquements de la pêche côtière et artisanale au niveau du port de Lmhiriz ont atteint 1.766 tonnes (T) à fin août 2026, en hausse de 31 % par rapport à la même période de l'année précédente, selon l'Office national des pêches (ONP). La valeur marchande de ces captures a progressé de 78 % à plus de 44,74 millions de dirhams (MDH) à fin août dernier, contre plus de 25,11 MDH à fin août 2025, a précisé l'ONP dans son dernier rapport sur les statistiques de la pêche côtière et artisanale au Maroc. Par espèce, les quantités de poissons pélagiques débarquées dans ce port ont diminué de 62 % au cours des huit premiers mois de cette année à 31 T, pour une valeur de 193.000 dirhams (-58 %), contre 462.000 DH/82 T à fin août 2025. Les débarquements des poissons blancs se sont, quant à eux, repliés de 36 % à 591 T, pour une valeur de plus de 7,93 MDH (-10 %), contre plus de 8,82 MDH/923 T une année auparavant. S'agissant des débarquements des céphalopodes, ils ont enregistré une hausse de 274 % à 1.027 T, pour une valeur de plus de 26,81 MDH (+187 %), tandis que pour les crustacés, les débarquements ont augmenté de 63 % à 117 T, générant des revenus de plus de 9,79 MDH (+51 %). Au niveau national, les débarquements des produits commercialisés de la pêche côtière et artisanale ont atteint 723.490 T à fin août dernier, en hausse de 6 % par rapport à la même période une année auparavant. En valeur, ces débarquements ont progressé de 1 % à plus de 7,44 milliards de dirhams (MMDH), contre plus de 7,37 MMDH en glissement annuel. The post Port de Lmhiriz : Bond de 78 % de la valeur des débarquements de la pêche à fin août appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Wawa/ Renforcement des infrastructures éducatives : Un bâtiment scolaire inauguré à Klabè-Adapé
items.description: Badou, 19 sept. (ATOP) –Un bâtiment scolaire a été inauguré le vendredi 18 septembre à l’École Primaire Publique (EPP) de Klabè-Adapé dans la commune Wawa 3. Le bâtiment est réalisé dans le cadre du Projet d’amélioration de la qualité et de l’équité de l’éducation de base (PAQEEB). Il est initié par le gouvernement, cette infrastructure moderne comprend trois salles de classe entièrement équipées en tables-bancs et bureaux pour enseignants. Elle est aussi composée d’un bureau de direction avec magasin, ainsi que de deux blocs sanitaires de trois cabines distinctes pour filles et garçons. L’ouvrage a été complété par un ensemble d’équipements d’entretien et de salubrité notamment outillage de nettoyage, poubelles, dispositifs de lavage des mains et fournitures d’hygiène, afin d’assurer un environnement d’apprentissage salubre et respectueux des normes d’hygiène. Le directeur régional de l’éducation Plateaux ouest, Sanla Mintchiébe, s’est félicité de l’aboutissement de ce projet qui répond à des doléances de la population. Il a invité l’ensemble des acteurs communautaires notamment enseignants, élèves et parents à prendre soins de ces installations, afin d’en garantir la pérennité. Le secrétaire général de la préfecture de Wawa, Assimadi Kanlampé, a souligné la portée des politiques publiques portées par le Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé en faveur du secteur éducatif. Il a exhorté les parents à soutenir activement le parcours scolaire de leurs enfants et a encouragé les apprenants à la discipline, à l’assiduité et à la recherche de l’excellence académique. La cérémonie d’inauguration, marquée par la coupure symbolique du ruban et une visite guidée des lieux, s’est déroulée en présence d’autorités administratives, communales et de notables. ATOP/PM/KKT/AR

items.title: Querelles de la majorité, Sebta, Mohamed Ouzzine dresse son bilan
items.description: Face aux fractures sociales, la désespérance de la jeunesse, les tensions et les défaillances au sein de la majorité, Mohamed Ouzzine, secrétaire général du Mouvement Populaire (MP), pose le diagnostic de la situation sociale et politique du pays. Dans une interview pour Hespress, et dans le sillage des élections législatives du 23 septembre, le chef du Mouvement populaire a abordé les prochaines échéances électorales, la crise des jeunes sans emplois, les tensions avec certains partis politiques espagnols depuis les événements de Sebta et la reddition des comptes, entre autres. Abordant les événements migratoires de Sebta le 30 et 31 juillet, Mohamed Ouzzine a déclaré que le MP a été le premier parti à réagir. Ce qui s'est passé, « nous ne l'avons pas exagéré et nous ne devons pas non plus le minimiser », a-t-il considéré. Pour le SG du Mouvement populaire, les événements migratoires de Sebta sont le résulta t « d'une perte d'espoir, conséquence de l'échec des politiques publiques ». Il a cité à ce titre, les chiffres dévoilés par le Conseil Economique, Social et Environnemental (CESE) sur les jeunes NEET (Not in Education, Employment, or Training), « des jeunes sans emploi, qui n'ont pas de formation adéquate, qui n'étudient pas, sans perspectives. C'est à dire, très éloignés du système social. Que faut-il attendre de la part de ces jeunes? Ils sont 4 millions et 300.000 (dans ce cas) et ça, j'en ai parlé à plusieurs reprises notamment au chef du gouvernement ». Ces jeunes, Ouzzine les a décrit comme une « bombe » dont les conséquences pourraient être subies par toute la population, selon lui. « On peut s'attendre à tout de leur part » , a-t-il affirmé, en se demandant ce qui a été fait pour leur cas, expliquant qu'il faut les encadrer, les rediriger vers la formation professionnelle rapide. Il a ainsi regretté ce qu'il a qualifié d'absence de décisions les concernant, ce qui aurait donné lieu, selon lui, à cette idée d' « opportunités dans une ville occupée -même si c'est une ville marocaine au demeurant- mais ils voient des opportunités dans cette ville malgré sa petite taille, et ils ne voient pas d'opportunités dans leur pays alors que notre pays est le pays des opportunités ». © Mounir Mehimdate « Il suffit qu'il y ait des politiques publiques attractives qui donnent une chance à ces jeunes pour qu'il voient cette opportunité », a-t-il estimé . Et d'ajouter: « Grâce à Dieu, nous avons l'un des plus beaux pays. On le voit, le monde est admiratif, mais l'absence de cette vitesse unique dont le Roi Mohammed VI a parlé en mentionnant les +deux vitesses+, c'est notre grand défi ». Dans le même sillage, Ouzzine a répondu à une question concernant le débat suscité en Espagne à la suite des événements de Sebta. Il a dit regretter que « les voisins du nord aient exploité la situation à des fins politiques internes », en mentionnant leurs échéances électorales à venir . Il a rappelé que les deux pays ont un « avenir commun » , se doivent de faire preuve de « bon voisinage » et a regretté les réactions qui manquent de « maturité » , rappelant que le dossier de la migration est un dossier « qui nous interpelle tous ». « Nous ne pouvons pas passer sous silence le rôle que joue le Royaume du Maroc dans cette question (de lutte contre la migration, ndlr) » , en soutenant qu'il s'agit d'un « défi majeur » et que le Maroc déploie des « efforts considérables » et de « lourds sacrifices » pour tenter de limiter cet afflux. © Mounir Mehimdate Concernant les interventions très fortes et prises de positions du MP face aux décisions gouvernementales (étant donné que le parti était dans l'opposition), Ouzzine a déclaré qu'elles émanaient de données et étaient basées sur des indicateurs, des chiffres issus d'institutions constitutionnelles. Le secrétaire général du Mouvement Populaire a critiqué ce qu'il a qualifié de « rupture illusoire » entre certaines composantes de la majorité, notamment le Rassemblement National des Indépendants (RNI) et le Parti Authenticité et Modernité (PAM). Il a estimé que ces derniers sont devenus, selon ses termes , « victimes de cette rupture artificielle », après avoir atteint le stade des invectives politiques au lieu de présenter un bilan clair aux Marocains. Sur le sujet des subventions octroyées pour la Fête du sacrifice, Ouzzine a refusé d'accuser une partie en particulier en affirmant ne pas avoir de preuves. « Ils (le gouvernement, ndlr) nous laissé en train de supposer. Nous (dans cette interview, ndlr) sommes en train de discuter sur une vérité dont nous n'avons pas de données » , a-t-il déclaré. © Mounir Mehimdate Au sujet des accusations croisées entre deux partis de la majorité gouvernementale sur le sujet, Ouzzine a souligné l'importance des commissions d'enquête parlementaires. Il a affirmé qu'en 2017, que le MP qui était en dans la majorité, a eu le « courage » de signer à la deuxième chambre du Parlement pour la mise en place d'une commission d'enquête parlementaire visant deux ministres de son propre parti, à savoir Mohand Laenser et Hakima El Haite. « Nous étions dans la majorité et nous avons signé! C'est ça le courage. Et là, nous leur demandons juste de voir les moutons. Si seulement, ils n'avaient rien dit. Chacun accuse l'autre, et nous voulions leur dire, venez (en commission d'enquête, ndlr) et dites nous qui est le fautif. Personne n'a pu nous répondre » , a-t-il déclaré. Et de là, le responsable au sein du Mouvement populaire, a insisté sur la nécessité de réformer le système de subventions. Estimant que ce sujet est intimement lié au pouvoir d'achat, Mohamed Ouzzine a déclaré: « Nous avons consacré beaucoup d'argent, mobilisé d'importantes sources financières en pensant que cela profiterait aux Marocains. Mais les Marocains n'ont pas vu les effets dans leur vie quotidienne », en signalant que cela englobait « les médicaments, la viande, le gasoil etc. » . Enfin, il a conclu son intervention, par un appel aux Marocains pour « voter en masse » et ne pas laisser de vide. « L'abstention ou le boycott ne sont pas une solution. Si la situation que vivent les Marocains ne leur convient pas, l'abstention et le boycott ne ferait qu'aggraver les choses, parce qu'aujourd'hui, ils ont le pouvoir de décision, ils peuvent voter pour ceux dont ils estiment que le programme et le projet répond à leurs attention et leur niveau d'exigence » , a-t-il affirmé. The post Querelles de la majorité, Sebta, Mohamed Ouzzine dresse son bilan appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: The Most Handsome Melon in Mexico? Yes, It’s a Real Contest.
Alphadjo Dara dévoile « Killi Killi », un nouveau clip placé sous le signe de l’amour
items.description: Le paysage musical guinéen s’enrichit d’un nouveau clip. Le célèbre artiste, chanteur et musicien guinéen Alphadjo Dara vient de dévoiler un nouveau morceau, intitulé « Killi Killi », une œuvre placée sous le signe de l’amour. Disponible sur la plateforme YouTube depuis ce samedi 19 septembre 2026, ce morceau constitue le premier extrait de son prochain album, qui « parle beaucoup d'amour, de joie de vivre et de paix », nous apprend-on. Fort d’une carrière jalonnée de plusieurs albums, Alphadjo Dara compte notamment à son actif « Bankitou Minata », sorti en 2000, « Soutoura », en 2002, « Djikké », en 2012, ainsi que « Kalifou » et « Ko djatta Nafata », sortis en 2020. À cette discographie s’ajoute une série de singles qui ont contribué à asseoir sa notoriété auprès du public guinéen. À travers ce nouveau clip, la figure emblématique de la musique pastorale guinéenne s’inscrit dans la droite ligne de sa vocation artistique, en mêlant harmonieusement les instruments traditionnels aux rythmes contemporains. Le tout est porté par une chorégraphie soignée et captivante, qui plonge le spectateur et le mélomane dans une atmosphère particulièrement chaleureuse. Originaire de Tougué, Alphadjo Dara fait de ce nouveau titre une rencontre entre l’authenticité de ses racines culturelles et les exigences de la création musicale contemporaine. Une démarche qui lui permet de renouer avec son univers artistique, tout en cherchant à séduire et à capter l’attention de ses nombreux fans. Mamadou Yaya Barry L’article Alphadjo Dara dévoile « Killi Killi », un nouveau clip placé sous le signe de l’amour est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .
